To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel ring-turnstile-LLP antenna configuration is introduced and demonstrated to have multi-octave bandwidth, dual CP and a miniaturization ratio of 2.5, which is the highest ever reported for a planar FI antenna.
the proposed ring-turnstile-LPs provide multi-octave operation and dual CP with size reductions of 2.5 and 3.2, respectively, relative to the baseline LPs.

the proposed ring-turnstile-LPs are novel, quasi-FI, dual-CP, and wide-bandwidth antennas that can be integrated with simple impedance matching networks and beamformers for use in a wide variety of wireless applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel quasi-FI antenna configuration that can be used in applications requiring wideband, low profile, and dual-CP operation.
the development of novel planar log-periodic antenna configurations with greatly enhanced bandwidths and dual CP operation.
the development of a novel antenna composite with a size reduction factor >2 and multi-octave operation in a planar configuration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a novel, simple, and efficient planar antenna configuration for wideband dual CP applications.
the ring-turnstile LP antenna has been successfully developed and demonstrated as a novel quasi FI, small size, dual CP, wideband antenna with potential for a variety of applications.

this novel ring-turnstile-LPB antenna is the first planar antenna to provide dual-CP operation and bandwidths as wide (multi-octave) as those of more complicated antennas such as sinuous and singly CP spirals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the novel ring-turnstile-LF antenna is a simple, small, low profile, dual-CP, and quasi-FI antenna that can be integrated with planar feeds to form a simple beamformer for multi-octave operation.
the ring-turnstile antenna concept is a promising alternative to spiral antennas, especially in applications where the bandwidth is a key requirement.
a simple, low profile, and low cost antenna is proposed and demonstrated for wideband, dual-CP, and unidirectional operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed ring-turnstile-LPs are capable of operating at frequencies below their cutoff frequency and are suitable for applications where wideband and small size are required.
the proposed concept of ring-turnstile-LPs can be utilized in a number of applications requiring wide bandwidth and/or small size.

the proposed ring-turnstile-LPs are capable of providing a wideband dual CP radiation pattern with a size reduction factor greater than 2.
